standard_prerequisites.name: Flatness, purity and the projection formula for a tt-functor with right adjoint
standard_prerequisites.reference: the author's Recollection T-S at source lines 722-749 and the citation to Balmer-DellAmbrogio-Sanders recorded in the source bibliography

core_obligations: For the inclusion of the image of the induced map into the support of U(unit): given C in the target homological spectrum and B the preimage of C, use that U is lax-monoidal so that the ring object U(unit) acts on U(E_C) in the big source category, apply the residue tensor functor h_B to obtain an action of h_B(U(unit)) on h_B(U(E_C)), and conclude that h_B(U(unit)) is non-zero because otherwise the injective hull of the unit in the residue category, which is a direct summand of h_B(U(E_C)) by the comparison lemma, would vanish (source lines 851-853).

For the converse direction: form the kernel I of the unit map into the injective hull in the residue category, transport it by the induced exact functor on module categories, and define the Serre tensor-ideal C_0 of finitely presented target modules annihilated by tensoring with the image of the injective hull (source lines 855-858).

Show that C_0 is proper: if it were everything then the image of the injective hull would vanish, hence the transport of I would be the unit; since I is the colimit of its finitely presented subobjects and the target unit is finitely presented, some finitely presented M inside I already maps onto the unit, and M lies in the localizing tensor-ideal generated by B, so that the projection formula gives M tensor U(unit) = U(unit) and hence the injective hull tensor U(unit) = 0, contradicting that B lies in the support of U(unit) (source line 859, first half).

Choose a maximal tensor-ideal C of the target containing C_0, observe that the preimage of C contains B and hence equals B by maximality, and conclude that B is the image of C under the induced map on homological spectra (source line 859, second half).

proof_roadmap.step: Rewrite the support of the ring object U(unit) as the naive support, using the theorem that the support of a weak ring is naive.
Inclusion: the ring U(unit) acts on U(E_C); if its residue image vanished then the injective hull of the unit, a summand of h_B(U(E_C)), would vanish.
Converse: build the Serre tensor-ideal C_0 from the kernel of the unit map into the injective hull and prove it proper by the projection formula.
Extend C_0 to a maximal tensor-ideal C and identify the preimage of C with B.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the theorem at source lines 844-848, label Thm:Spc-image, printed as Theorem 5.12: for a coproduct-preserving tensor-triangulated functor F between big tt-categories with right adjoint U, the image of the induced map on homological spectra is exactly the support of the ring object U(unit), and consequently the image on triangular spectra is its image under the comparison map. The proof at source lines 850-860 runs two genuinely different arguments. For the inclusion it uses that U is lax-monoidal, so that U(unit) acts on U(E_C), and that the pure-injective E_B is a direct summand of U(E_C) by the preceding comparison lemma, so that vanishing of the residue image of U(unit) would kill the injective hull of the unit in the residue abelian category. For the converse it forms the Serre tensor-ideal C_0 of finitely presented target modules annihilated by tensoring with the transported injective hull, proves C_0 proper by an ab absurdo argument in which the colimit description of the kernel together with finite presentability of the target unit produce a finitely presented M in the localizing tensor-ideal generated by B, and the projection formula turns M tensor U(unit) = U(unit) into the vanishing of the injective hull tensor U(unit); a maximal tensor-ideal containing C_0 then has preimage exactly B. Neither direction follows from the definition of support: flatness of the residue functors, the injective-hull comparison across Gabriel quotients and the projection formula are all used essentially.
